title: Police and housing protesters clash in Lisbon and Porto
seoTitle: Lisbon housing and police clash protests

tea.why: Protesters are demonstrating against Portugal's severe housing crisis and a rental bill making evictions easier and ending rent caps.
tea.want: Demonstrators are calling on the government to scrap plans that would make evictions easier and end rent caps on new leases.
tea.changed: Nov 1: Police cleared protest camps in Lisbon and Porto, leading to 13 arrests and multiple reported injuries.

summary: Housing protesters in Lisbon and Porto set up tents in public squares following marches against soaring housing costs and government rental legislation. Police subsequently moved in to dismantle the camps in Lisbon's Rossio Square and Porto's Dom Joao I Square. Authorities used shields, batons, and crowd control methods to disperse demonstrators, resulting in clashes where some participants reportedly threw bottles and paint at officers. Police stated that 13 people were arrested and 13 officers were injured during the operations. Activist groups and lawyers criticized the police response as excessive, while a fresh rally was called in the capital.
demands: Scrap plans that make evictions easier
End rent caps on new leases
response: Police used shields, batons, and tear gas to clear protest camps, resulting in 13 arrests. According to police, 13 officers were injured and an unspecified number of civilians were also hurt during the clashes. Prime Minister Luis Montenegro ruled out withdrawing the bill.

arrests.text: Six people were arrested in Lisbon and seven in Porto

injuries.text: 13 police were injured as they tried to take down the camps, with eight taken to hospital

updates.text: Police cleared protest camps in Rossio Square in Lisbon and Dom Joao I Square in Porto, leading to clashes and 13 arrests.

sources.title: Clashes broke out in Portugal as police stormed housing protest camps in Lisbon and Porto
